title: Rapid redistribution talent pool and 48hr coverage protocol
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight tactical runbook for mobilizing a prequalified bench (internal+contractor) and closing critical coverage gaps within 48 hours. Designed for small-to-medium urgent needs: emergency backfills, short-term cross-functional coverage, and incident-driven surges where product/business continuity matters.

Scope / when to invoke (quick checklist):
- Invoke when a role that supports production/ops/customer SLAs will be vacant for >24h and cannot be covered by existing rota.
- Use for coverage windows up to 30 days; for longer assignments, transition to normal hiring cadence.
- Not for standard planned hires, performance-managed exits, or roles with >60-day lead time.

Stakeholders:
- People Ops (owner): Sophie Chen
- Hiring manager: (fills in)
- On-call lead / SRE manager: (if infra coverage)
- Procurement / vendor ops: Miguel Alvarez (contractor fast-track)
- Legal: as needed for contractor addenda

Trigger timeline (48hr target):
T=0 (trigger): Hiring manager opens PEOPLE-482 emergency ticket (template below) and pings #people-ops-emergency.
- People Ops ack within 1 hour. Assign PoP owner.
T=0-6h: Rapid triage call (15–30m) to agree scope of coverage, minimum viable skill set (MVS), and ramp expectations.
T=6-18h: Candidate pool activation: internal transfers first, then pre-vetted contractors, then expedited external outreach.
T=18-30h: Short screening loop: 30–45m technical/behavioral + 15m hiring manager sync. Use the quick rubric below.
T=30-42h: Selection, offer (contractor PO), and access provisioning kick-off.
T=42-48h: Handoff + role-specific shadowing (2–6h) + live pairing with incumbent or buddy.

Rapid triage questions (to define MVS):
- Essential tasks the person must do on day 1 (list 3).
- Systems and credentials required (SRE keys, dashboard access, pager duty).
- Minimum acceptable outcome after 48h (ex: triage queue cleared, two customer incidents closed).
- Who is the staging buddy for first 48h?

Candidate funnel and prioritization: 
1) Internal volunteers/transfers (fastest, avoids offboarding friction).
2) Preapproved contractors from vendor roster (have NDAs and SOWs).
3) Former employees in the alumni pool (rehire shortlists).
4) External temp staffing (last resort).

Quick screening rubric (30–45m):
- Core competency (50%): demonstrated on-call / production troubleshooting experience relevant to scope. Scale: 0–5.
- Practical test (30%): Give a short scenario (2–4 bullet steps). Candidate explains triage plan. Scale: 0–5.
- Communication & escalation (20%): clear instructions, escalation judgement. Scale: 0–5.
Pass threshold: weighted score >=3.6 (out of 5).

Handoff template (to deliver to incoming):
- Role summary (1 paragraph).
- Critical runbooks & dashboards (links).
- Active incidents / open tickets with owners and priority.
- Pager expectations, overlap windows, contact tree.
- Minimal set of credentials/access and the request path.
- First 6–12 hour goals.
- Known risks and mitigation steps.

48hr onboarding checklist (minimum MVP):
- HR: contractor PO signed or internal transfer approved.
- IT/Security: temporary access created (expires at 30d default).
- Tools: Slack channel invite, PagerDuty override, Okta group assignment.
- Role buddy assigned and 2-4h shadow scheduled.
- First tasks queued and verified in ticketing system.
- Quick health check scheduled at 24h and 48h.

Communication templates (short):
- Slack (to #people-ops-emergency): 
"EMERGENCY COVERAGE: PEOPLE-482 opened for [role]. MVS: [3 bullets]. PO owner @Sophie. Triage call in 30m. Need volunteer/contractor by EOD."
- Manager -> candidate offer (contractor):
"Hi [name], we have an immediate 48h coverage role to start ASAP. Scope: [one-liner]. Pay/SOW terms: [TBD]. Can you start within 48h? Please reply with availability and confirmation of prior system experience."

Risk & compliance notes (short):
- Security: limit blast radius—create time-bound credentials and avoid sharing long-lived keys.
- Contractors must sign the standard emergency SOW and NDAs before system access.
- For regulated data access, escalate to Legal & Security; consider role-lite coverage (no PII access) if necessary.

Success metrics (how we judge a run):
- Coverage time: target <=48h from trigger to first shift started.
- Triage resolution: initial incident queue reduced by >=60% within 24h of coverage start.
- Manager satisfaction: quick poll at 72h (NPS-style).

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Default pay rates for <7d contractor surges (who signs off?) -> propose People Ops & Finance preapprove 3 tiers.
- Automation: can we wire a small PagerDuty-to-PeopleOps alert to seed the ticket automatically? (POC: PEOPLE-488)
- Should we create a persistent 6-person standby roster for Q1 2026? (budget impact)

Operational notes & quick links:
- Related Confluence: CONFLUENCE:HR/rapid-coverage-playbook
- Tracking JIRA epic: PEOPLE-482 (emergency coverage experiments)
- Slack channel: #people-ops-emergency
- Vendor roster doc: /shared/vendor/contractors-approved.csv (procurement)

Retro & follow-up cadence after each event (recommended):
- 72h retro: 15–30m to capture what worked, blockers, and access issues.
- 2-week post-mortem to decide whether role needs long-term hire or extended contract.
- Update prequalified roster entries and lessons in the Confluence playbook.

Notes to self (Sophie):
- Try a dry-run in November with an internal transfer exercise; simulate 24h window.
- Ask Finance to pre-authorize three pay bands for emergency usage.

Draft templates and minimal artifacts attached (move to Confluence when stable).

-- end of draft --

Unresolved fragments / TODOs (stream-of-consciousness):
- Shortlist names from alumni list (Noah to pull)
- Confirm whether Okta supports 48h expiring sessions by default
- Add example SOW language for 72h engagements
summary: Tactical runbook to close critical coverage gaps within 48 hours using internal transfers and pre-vetted contractors. Includes trigger timeline, rapid screening rubric, onboarding checklist, templates, risks, and follow-up cadence.
